शकट, probably for शक् + अत्र,
 I. m., f. टी, and n. A cart, Hit. i. d. 89, M.M. (n.); Pañc. 8, 15 (ता);

(टी); with प्राजापत्य, name of an asterism, Pañc. i. d. 239 (टा).
 II. m.
 1. A cart-load.
 2. A Daitya slain by Kṛṣṇa.
 III. m. or n.
 1. An implement for preparing grain,

. A form of marching an army, 7, 187.
 --Comp.

शकार, m. A silly brother-in-law of a king.

. []
 3. Impers. pass. To be fit to be done,
. The pass. transfers its pass. signification to the infin. which it governs, e. g. न शक्यन्ते नियन्तुम्,
, M.M. (नीतिं ग्राहयितुं शक्यन्ते, They are able to be taught good behaviour); with a ptcple. of the pass. of the Caus. instead of the infin., न शक्यते निवर्त्यमाना,

(She cannot be induced to return).

(They can be guarded).

शक,
 1. m. pl. The name of a people,

. A particular caste.
 3. An era, especially that of Śālivāhana, commencing seventy-six or seventy-eight years after the Christian.

 I. (m. and) n. A potherb, any vegetable,

; Hit. i. d. 67, M.M.
 II. m.
 1.

. One of the seven द्वीपस्.
 3. An era, especially that of Śālivāhana, beginning seventy-six or seventyeight years after the Christian.
 --Comp.
(? perhaps to be corrected to शकज, A man of Śaka, i. e. Scythic extraction, or a proper name).

शकटार, m.
 1. A bird of prey (a vulture?), Hit. ii. d. 97.
 2. and शकटाल शकटाल, A proper name,

 --Comp.
शकलिन्, i. e. शकल + इन्, m. A fish.

शक् + उन (or rather शक् + वन् + अ, cf. शकुन्त),

शाकुन, i. e. शकुन + अ, adj.
 1. Of or relating to birds.

शक् + उनि (see the last),
 I. m.
 1. A bird, Pañc. iii. d. 140.
 2. The Indian kite, Falco cheela.
 3. A surname of the Aśvins,

.
 II. f. नी, A hensparrow.
 --Probably akin to O.N. haukr; Danish, hog; O.H.G. habuh; A.S. hafoe.

शक् + उन्त (or rather शक् + वन्त् + अ, cf. शकुन), m.
 1. A bird, Pañc. i. d. 155.
 2. The Indian vulture.
 3. The blue jay.
शकुन्त + क, m., f. तिका, A bird, Utt.

शकुन्त + ला, f. A proper name, Śāk. 3, 5.
 --Comp.
शकुन्ति (cf. शकुन्त), m. A bird, Utt.

.
 --Cf. σκώρ, σκατός, σκέρ-βολος; A.S. scearn; perhaps Lat. stercus and cerda in su-cerda (rather to शृध्?), etc.; and Goth. spai-skuldrs, Spittle.

स-कृ + त्, adv.
 1. Once, Vikr. d. 10.

 1. Strength, Pañc. i. d. 265; with loc.,

(of the god of love); eight particular goddesses, ब्राह्मी, etc. cf. Wilson, Hind.
